entry.title: fix(config/validation): allow `datasource-releases-*` in `cacheTtlOve…
entry.content:
fix(config/validation): allow `datasource-releases-*` in `cacheTtlOverride` (#48035)

* fix(config/validation): allow `datasource-releases-*` in `cacheTtlOverride`

As a follow-up to 321965a7fa2c3cd8b7cf275d5ad2860ab5300a3d, where we
started validating that `cacheTtlOverride` keys are valid namespaces,
we didn't include the namespace each datasource caches its releases in,
`datasource-releases-{datasource}`.

This namespace isn't in the list of namespaces we validate against, as
it's built from the datasource's ID, but its TTL can be overridden.

This led to `renovate-config-validator` failing for a config that works,
i.e.:

    cacheTtlOverride: namespace `datasource-releases-npm` does not exist

We can build the namespaces from the list of datasources, so we still
flag a datasource which doesn't exist, and use them in the JSON schema,
too.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <jamie.tanna+amp@mend.io>

* fixup! fix(config/validation): allow `datasource-releases-*` in `cacheTtlOverride`

entry.title: feat(json-schema): only allow known `cacheTtlOverride` namespaces (#4…
entry.content:
feat(json-schema): only allow known `cacheTtlOverride` namespaces (#48034)

As a follow-up to 321965a7fa2c3cd8b7cf275d5ad2860ab5300a3d, where we
started validating that `cacheTtlOverride` keys are valid namespaces,
we should also make this visible in the JSON schema.

This provides better auto-complete, and in-editor validation when
specifying an incorrect namespace.

This still allows a glob/regex pattern.

entry.title: fix(gerrit): a push fails with "Missing tree" when the target branch …
entry.content:
fix(gerrit): a push fails with "Missing tree" when the target branch moved since the last fetch (#48168)

* fix(gerrit): a push fails with "Missing tree" when the target branch moved since the last fetch

* fix(gerrit): a failed fetch of the target branch prevents the push

* fix(gerrit): disable tag following on the fetch before push

Git followed no tags on this fetch only because its refspec has no
destination, a rule of git's fetch implementation that the git-fetch
documentation does not state. `--no-tags` keeps the fetch from writing
into refs/tags/* even if git changes that rule.
